Tests can be useful towards resolving issues on code repositories. However, relying too much on tests for issue resolution can lead to code that technically passes observed tests but actually misses important cases or even breaks functionality. t to tests t gen t_{\textrm{gen}} generated using the same LLM? RQ2. How does refining code c new c_{\textrm{new}} based on observed tests t gen t_{\textrm{gen}} affect test overfitting? RQ3. If the hidden tests t gold t_{\textrm{gold}} were revealed, would refining code based on them break other functionality? Our experiments use two LLMs, Claude-3.7 Sonnet and GPT-4o. We use strong existing LLM-based systems as a starting point, obtaining the candidate code c new c_{\textrm{new}} from Agentless ( Xia et al., 2025 ) and the surrogate test t gen t_{\textrm{gen}} from e-Otter++ ( Ahmed et al., 2026 ) . The experiments are based on the TDD-bench Verified ( Ahmed et al., 2024 ) benchmark for test-driven development, which is derived from SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) . Conclusion In this work, we systematically show that test overfitting is still a problem in LLM-based program repair. We also show that test-based refinement may resolve some additional issues but increases overfitting. Therefore, using tests for patch generation needs more deliberation.
